Key observations: the kernel computes rho(x) via the algebraically equivalent form x²/(sqrt(1+x²)+1) instead of the problem's stated sqrt(1+x²)−1 — an explicit rewrite the contract permits. Notable numeric detail: x is FP16 cast to FP32, so x*x is exact in FP32 (11-bit×11-bit mantissa ≤ 24 bits), and both sqrt and div_rn are correctly rounded in FP32, giving only a few ulps of error against a 1e-5 relative / 1e-8 absolute tolerance. The rational form also avoids the catastrophic cancellation that sqrt(1+x²)−1 would suffer for tiny x, and square of ±65504 (~4.29e9) is well inside FP32 range.

The tolerance abs 1e-8 is tight for small x². FP32 division of tiny square by ~2: relative error ~1e-7 of x², which is ~2e-7·rho — relative tolerance is 1e-5·rho, fine. Extreme x=65504: square = 4.29e9 fits in FP32 (max 3.4e38), fine. sqrt(1+square): sqrt(4.29e9)=65504.x — catastrophic cancellation is avoided by the rational form; actually kernel form avoids cancellation. Reference uses same rational form in FP64 — matches well. Looks likely correct; main risk is FP32 rounding precision vs 1e-5 relative tolerance: FP32 has ~1e-7 relative precision, division correctly rounded (div_rn), sqrt IEEE. square = x*x exact? x is FP16 converted to FP32, x*x in FP32: product of FP16 values, 11-bit mantissas → product has ≤22 bits, exactly representable in FP32 (24 bits). So square exact. 1+square fine. sqrt correctly rounded. root+1 rounding. division correctly rounded. Total error ~2-3 ulp relative ~2-4e-7, well within 1e-5. Seems correct.
